title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.intervention: Addition of ~5 at.% Re via arc‐melting and homogenization, followed by heavy‐ion irradiation to ~1 dpa at 600 °C (guess)
recollection.structure: Single‐phase BCC solid solution with slight lattice parameter expansion and indications of short‐range Re ordering (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Re atoms segregate to point‐defect clusters, reducing defect mobility and promoting vacancy–interstitial recombination to suppress void nucleation (guess)
recollection.results: Re‐doped alloy displayed ~30% lower swelling and ~20% reduced defect density under 1 dpa irradiation at 600 °C compared to the base NbMoTaW alloy (guess)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies Re addition and a single-phase BCC alloy only at a broad level, but the claimed 5 at.% Re, arc melting, homogenization, heavy-ion irradiation, 1 dpa, and 600 °C are wrong. It misses the sputtered equiatomic NbMoTaWRe films and 120 keV He implantation. The proposed recombination mechanism is directionally related but attributes it to unsupported Re segregation and reduced defect mobility, missing grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and suppression of He-bubble segregation. All quantitative swelling and defect-density results are invented.
